norms.definition: The model specifies coordinate ranges of finite vectors. Discrete action labels have no derivative order. A placeholder norm imposes no additional geometric assumption.

objects.definition: Arm reward distributions are fixed, unknown, and supported on $[0,1]$, with a unique best arm. The arm count $K$, budget $T$, and bound $h$ are public, and $H(\nu)=\sum_{i\ne b}(\mu_b-\mu_i)^{-2}\le h$. Neither the actual gaps nor $H$ are revealed.
The mean μ_i belongs to the ith fixed reward distribution. It is unknown and cannot be queried directly.

protocols.adversary_information: The unknown distribution or parameter is fixed before interaction. Learner randomness and sample randomness are independent. No adversary changes the distribution round by round from the learner's history.
protocols.loss_bearing_points: There is no regret-incurring action point; every arm pull consumes the fixed T budget.
protocols.past_requery: No new information may be requested from past rounds or previously used samples. Received feedback may be stored and processed. In a stochastic model, an action may be repeated in a new round, with a fresh charged sample.
protocols.queries_per_round: Use a fixed number $T$ of arm pulls and compare error probability, not expected stopping time.
steps: The environment fixes an admissible ν. The learner receives K, T, and h.
At each time $t=1,\ldots,T$, select an arm using past feedback and draw one fresh sample.
Recommend one arm after exactly T calls.
Performance is error-event probability. There is no cumulative-regret objective.
